watchList.thisSessionStatus: Found FIVE ADDITIONAL, UNDOCUMENTED collisions this session by cross-referencing every real super(orgId, "agentId", supabase) literal in src/lib/agents/*.ts against the registry: AG-02 (registry 'eligibility_scoring' vs. orphaned, unwired EligibilityScoringAgent using literal 'ag-02'), AG-08 (registry 'ag-08-nofa-parser' vs. unregistered-but-scheduled RenewalTrackerAgent using literal 'ag-08-renewal-tracker'), AG-09 (registry 'email_parser' vs. unregistered-but-scheduled OutcomeAnalyzerAgent using literal 'ag-09-outcome-analyzer'), AG-10 (registry 'ag-10-grant-dna' vs. unregistered-but-scheduled DocumentExpiryAgent using literal 'ag-10-document-expiry'), AG-11 (registry 'cold_outreach' vs. unregistered-but-scheduled KnowledgeGapAgent using literal 'ag-11-knowledge-gap'), AG-12 (registry 'ag-12-autoapply' vs. unregistered-but-scheduled SearchProfileOptimizerAgent using literal 'ag-12-search-optimizer'). worker/autonomous-orchestrator.ts's own header comment (lines 6-44) independently corroborates every one of these as deliberate code-level labeling ('requested X -> Y (AG-N, exact match)'), so these are not accidental typos — they are real, live, SCHEDULED agents running nightly/monthly/weekly inside runOrgPipeline() under a canonical number the registry has already assigned to a completely different agent. A future Agent Log Viewer or any tooling that joins agent_registry.agent_id against agent_runs.agent_type will misattribute or drop these five agents' real run history entirely. Also found: EligibilityScoringAgent (agentId 'ag-02') is REAL CODE but has NO production instantiation anywhere except a dev/test script (scripts/ff-agent-test.ts) — dead code sharing a canonical number with a live agent, not merely a naming collision. Also found: three separate real budget-generating implementations (budget-agent.ts, budget-builder.ts — both literally 'budget_builder' — and budget-builder-agent.ts — 'ag-06-budget-builder') were not individually disambiguated this pass.
watchList.priority: HIGH — this is a structural data-integrity gap in the registry itself (6+ real agents are invisible to any registry-driven tooling), not a cosmetic naming issue. Recommend the deep test confirm real agent_runs row counts under each colliding literal to size the actual blast radius (how much history is currently mis-joined or orphaned).
